faq.q: What was Brown v Board of Education?
faq.a: A 1954 US Supreme Court case that ruled separate schools for Black and white children unconstitutional. It overturned the idea of separate but equal in public education.
asks: What ended school segregation in the USA?

faq.a: A Black civil rights activist and seamstress in Montgomery, Alabama. On 1 December 1955 she refused to give up her bus seat to a white man and was arrested, sparking the bus boycott.

faq.q: What was the Montgomery bus boycott?
faq.a: A protest from 5 December 1955 to 20 December 1956, in which Black residents of Montgomery refused to ride the city's segregated buses. It lasted 381 days.
asks: How long did the bus boycott last?

faq.q: How did the bus boycott end?
faq.a: In the case Browder v Gayle, courts ruled that bus segregation was unconstitutional, and the US Supreme Court upheld this in November 1956. The boycott ended when the order took effect in December 1956.

faq.q: What did the Civil Rights Act of 1964 do?
faq.a: This US law banned discrimination based on race, colour, religion, sex or national origin, and ended legal segregation in public places like restaurants, hotels and workplaces.
asks: What was the Civil Rights Act?

facts: The Montgomery bus boycott lasted 381 days, from 5 December 1955 to 20 December 1956.
Rosa Parks was arrested on 1 December 1955.
The US Civil Rights Act was signed in July 1964.
